analysis.title: US midterms: Blue wave ushers in gridlock (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: Democrats are projected by the AP and major TV networks to retake both the House and Senate, ending unified Republican control of Washington. The scale of the win exceeded what markets had priced before election day.

UBS reads the result as a referendum on the incumbent administration, consistent with negative presidential approval ratings and elevated oil prices. It cautions against reading it as a broad Democratic policy mandate.

UBS expects legislative friction rather than sharp policy change. President Trump keeps veto power, Senate rules and divided government constrain sweeping tax or spending bills, and the executive branch keeps broad authority over tariffs and foreign policy.

Democratic control gives oversight of the administration, confirmation authority over appointments, more influence over spending and debt-limit talks, and a platform to test policy on social security, health care and AI regulation ahead of 2028.
Trump suggested he will work with Democrats and does not want to veto everything. UBS thinks markets pricing in 2028 outcomes is premature and expects investors to refocus on fundamentals.

Debt talks are the clearest risk for bonds. The 2027 debt-ceiling negotiations could soften scheduled social-program cuts and raise defense spending, which could reverse an expected narrowing in deficits and increase Treasury supply. Brinkmanship could raise bond volatility.
UBS still expects inflation to moderate, the Federal Reserve to finish raising rates, and Treasury yields to settle lower.

Congressional oversight of AI is not expected to derail the AI investment cycle. Broad federal restrictions face legislative and presidential constraints, and state and local rules matter more for data center timing and location, including the Texas result.

UBS raised its aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027. Investors are weighting overinvestment, financing and monetization risks more, and higher volatility could become the new normal.

Positioning guidance: a more definitive Democratic outcome could drive near-term volatility in tech and regulation-sensitive areas, but UBS sees no need for an immediate strategic shift. It uses politically driven weakness to rebalance or build exposure gradually.

UBS keeps a constructive equity view on strong earnings. It advises reducing single-stock concentration, rebalancing oversized tech exposure, and tilting toward quality companies across the AI value chain.

UBS sees attractive income and diversification in high-quality bonds, particularly short- to medium-term maturities. Persistent deficits and heavy issuance underpin caution toward the longest maturities.

sector_views.rationale: AI infrastructure demand is strong and earnings support the equity view. UBS favors quality companies and financially strong platforms and infrastructure providers across the AI value chain, while advising a rebalance of oversized tech exposure and expecting near-term volatility from regulatory scrutiny.

sector_views.sector: Fixed income (short- to medium-term high-quality bonds)
sector_views.rationale: Current yields offer attractive income and diversification. UBS is cautious on the longest maturities because of persistent deficits and heavy issuance.

earnings_insights: UBS says strong earnings support its constructive view on equities. The report gives no company-level figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields fell after the midterm results. UBS expects Treasury yields to settle lower over time but flags debt-ceiling talks and heavier issuance as the main bond risk.
UBS raised its forecasts, which supports its view that AI infrastructure demand remains strong despite investor concern over overinvestment and financing.

macro_indicators.reading: Fed expected to finish raising rates
macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS expects the tightening cycle to end and inflation to moderate, which supports lower Treasury yields.
Japanese tech shares fell on the initial reaction. Sentiment then improved, with European markets broadly up.
US equity futures were modestly higher after the midterm results.

risk_factors: 2027 debt-ceiling negotiations could reverse the expected narrowing in deficits and increase Treasury supply.
Bond market volatility from political brinkmanship in 2027.
Investor concern over AI overinvestment, financing and monetization.
State and local rules, including the Texas result, could affect data center projects.
Greater regulatory scrutiny of tech and AI after the Democratic win.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects near-term volatility in tech and other regulation-sensitive areas after the more definitive Democratic outcome.
AI-related volatility may pick up on politics, and higher volatility could become the new normal for AI.
Brinkmanship over the 2027 debt ceiling could raise bond market volatility.
UBS advises using politically driven weakness to rebalance or build exposure gradually rather than abandon long-term positions.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democrats projected to win the House and Senate, ending unified Republican control of Washington.
Elevated oil prices and negative presidential approval ratings cited as drivers of the vote.
The executive branch retains broad authority over tariffs and foreign policy despite the change in Congress.
